verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: Plug the appliance or device (the load) you want to control into the module's outlet, with the load's own switch in the on position.
Plug the module into an unswitched outdoor wall outlet protected by a ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI).
steps.expect: Status LED turns on solid green

steps.text: If the load does not turn on, tap the SET button.
Let the module hang down from the outlet so it faces down.

notes: Use a 3-prong outlet with GFCI protection, or one protected by a GFCI device upstream; do not plug into a switched outlet, a filtered power strip or an AC line filter.
After installation the load's own switch no longer controls it unless load sensing is enabled.

steps.text: Use the SET button to set the module to the state you want the controller to activate (on or off).
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps (3 seconds).
steps.expect: Double beep; Status LED turns solid green if the load is on or solid red if it is off

notes: The module links as a responder: set the controller to linking mode first (for most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds or the SET button for 3 seconds), then press and hold this module's SET button.

Pressing and holding the SET button for 3 seconds on its own puts the module in linking mode (Status LED blinks green) for four minutes; the Outdoor On/Off Module 2456S3E Owner's Manual uses this to assign an X10 address.
Tap the SET button to leave a setup mode; a long beep means the module timed out of setup mode.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps (3 seconds).
steps.expect: Double beep; Status LED turns solid green if the load is on or solid red if it is off

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder; the device makes no link back to the Hub, since this profile lists no group it controls.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: With the controller in unlinking mode, press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps (3 seconds).
steps.expect: Status LED turns solid green if the load is on or solid red if it is off

notes: To unlink, set the controller to unlinking mode first (for most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds twice or the SET button for 3 seconds twice), then press and hold this module's SET button for 3 seconds.
Pressing and holding the SET button for 3 seconds twice puts the module itself in unlinking mode (Status LED blinks red).

steps.text: Unlink the module from any controller that controls it.
Unplug the module.
Wait about 10 seconds.
While holding down the SET button, plug the module back in without letting go of the button.
steps.expect: Module beeps and the Status LED turns solid green

steps.text: Keep holding the SET button for 3 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes red and then turns solid green; after a few seconds the load turns on

steps.text: Unlink the module from every controller it is linked to.

notes: The Outdoor On/Off Module 2456S3E Owner's Manual says to unlink the module from all controllers before you stop using it; otherwise the controllers keep retrying commands and slow the system.
If an X10 primary address was assigned, remove it as well.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove the modem's group 0 link with no SET button press: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
